chase_cards.name: Crystal Tower's Entei [CoroCoro jumbo insert]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not only an Entei card; it is an oversized movie-location card. The object carries CoroCoro distribution, the third-movie tower apparatus, and a computer-graphic Entei image into one jumbo paper artifact.

key_artists.name: CR CG gangs
key_artists.why: CR CG gangs matters because this card is explicitly architectural and cinematic. The illustration credit fits the object: a jumbo card about a crystalline movie tower rendered through a computer-graphic studio lane rather than a hand-drawn creature portrait lane.

claims.text: The local catalog models the CoroCoro Comic August 2000 insert source group as one row containing Crystal Tower's Entei at source index 193, with Jumbo as the variant note.
Bulbapedia says Crystal Tower's Entei was available in Japan as a Jumbo Unnumbered Promotional card on an insert in the August 2000 issue of CoroCoro Comic, released on July 15, 2000.
Bulbapedia says the movie Spell of the Unown: Entei was originally released in Japan as Lord of the Unknown Tower: Entei on July 8, 2000.

Bulbapedia says the top-left border text identifies the card as the Theater version Pocket Monsters 2000 Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei special jumbo card, and that Jumbo cards cannot be used at official tournaments.

Bulbapedia says the bottom border text identifies the card as a CoroCoro Comic August issue supplement, and that the CoroCoro Comic and Pikachu the Movie 2000 logos appear on the card with the CoroCoro dragon mascot in place of an expansion symbol.
Bulbapedia identifies CR CG gangs as the illustrator for Crystal Tower's Entei, and PokeBoon also lists CR CG Gangs for the CoroCoro jumbo promo.

Bulbapedia describes CR CG gangs as the credited artist for multiple Unnumbered Promotional cards including Crystal Tower's Entei, Pichu, Pikachu, Suicune, and Larvitar, and says the card design credits were Creatures, Inc. and Ryuta Kusumi.

As interpretive art context, the CR CG gangs credit is unusually important on Crystal Tower's Entei because the card foregrounds a constructed movie place and theatrical architecture as much as the legendary Pokemon.
Bulbapedia identifies Crystal Tower's Entei as a Fire-type Basic Pokemon card with 120 HP and the Tackle and Fire Spin attacks.
Bulbapedia says Crystal Tower's Entei is a promotional addition to the Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei collection and was never released in English.

As judged collector texture, the CoroCoro Crystal Tower's Entei jumbo matters because it turns the third movie's crystalline setting into an oversized card object, making the place, promotion, and legendary Pokemon inseparable.

narrative.human_title: CoroCoro Crystal Tower's Entei: the movie tower made jumbo
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those promos where the title is the map. It is not merely Entei; it is Crystal Tower's Entei, a jumbo CoroCoro object carrying the third movie's architecture, logos, border text, and theatrical timing. CR CG gangs makes sense here because the card is partly about spectacle and construction: a legendary Pokemon inside a manufactured crystal place, scaled up for a magazine reader's hands.
not_claiming: that every Entei listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says Crystal Tower's Entei, Entei jumbo, CoroCoro August 2000, Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei, Spell of the Unown, Pikachu the Movie 2000, CR CG gangs, or Japanese unnumbered promo row 193.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat Crystal Tower's Entei as a movie-location jumbo card identity. Establish the CoroCoro August 2000 insert route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is Crystal Tower's Entei and that the claimed route is the August 2000 CoroCoro Comic insert released July 15, 2000.
Confirm the physical format is Jumbo. Do not collapse this into a normal-size Entei card, Premium File 2 Entei, Awakening Legends Entei, Wind from the Sea Entei, or another Entei promo.
Look for top-left border text identifying the Theater version Pocket Monsters 2000 Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei special jumbo card.
Look for bottom border text identifying the CoroCoro Comic August issue supplement.
Check for the CoroCoro Comic and Pikachu the Movie 2000 logos, and the CoroCoro dragon mascot in place of an expansion symbol.

Keep the movie route legible: this is tied to the third movie / Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei apparatus, not the theatrical-release Hitmontop and Igglybuff promo pair or ordinary Entei set cards.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual jumbo card, including format/scale evidence, top-left and bottom border text, logo/mascot area, front/back, surface, edge/corner condition, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that Entei name alone identifies the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

narrative.human_title: Crystal Tower's Entei: the giant movie-place card
narrative.why_it_matters: This card asks the collector to look at more than the Pokemon. The name pins Entei to the Crystal Tower, the jumbo scale makes the card behave like a poster, and the CoroCoro route keeps it inside the magazine/movie machine of summer 2000. It is one of those objects where the apparatus is the identity: border text, logos, tower, mascot, movie title, and oversized format all matter.
not_claiming: that every Entei print follows this route
